title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A 'courbe spéciale épinglée par G' is a stable nodal curve over a base S, rigidified by an identification of its dual graph with a fixed graph G. Vertices carry genera; edges are nodes; legs are marked points. M_G is the moduli 'multiplicité modulaire' (Grothendieck's term for an algebraic stack) of such G-pinned curves. On the stability locus, M_G is a boundary stratum of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification, rigidified by the pinning.

The previous page defines the 'découpe' of G along a set C of edges: each edge in C is cut at its midpoint, and the two half-edges become marked points (legs). This gives a morphism (of 'numérotations' or 'normalisation') G' → G. Geometrically, a G-pinned curve is normalised at the nodes indexed by C, which yields canonically a G'-pinned curve. This gives the functor (131) M_G(S) → M_{G'}(S).

This page:
- The functor (131) is compatible with base change, so it defines a morphism of stacks (132) M_G → M_{G'}, provided G and G' are stable.
- Composition behaves functorially, so G ↦ M_G is a contravariant functor on stable graphs with normalisation morphisms.
- Proposition (a): if G → G' is a strict normalisation morphism, (132) is an isomorphism of stacks. With the pinning, normalising and re-gluing the paired marked points are mutually inverse.
- Proposition (b): if G is the disjoint sum of stable graphs G_α, then M_G → ∏_α M_{G_α} is an isomorphism (133). A curve with disconnected dual graph is just a tuple of curves.
- Grothendieck then overwrites M_G by Π_1 M_G, the (profinite) fundamental groupoid. The marginal NB says he will replace M_G by Π_1 M_G, with a variant of the product.
- Corollary (finished on the next page): G ↦ Π_1 M_G is a contravariant functor on stable graphs for normalisation morphisms. It sends strict ones to equivalences of groupoids and commutes with products.
- Next page: taking the minimal strict sub-object (full normalisation) gives (144), Π_1 M_G ≃ ∏_{vertices α} Π_1 M_{g_α, I_α}. That is, the fundamental groupoid of a boundary stratum splits as a product of fundamental groupoids of the lower-dimensional moduli stacks attached to the vertices.

Purpose: this is the combinatorial and functorial skeleton of the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν}, i.e. the Teichmüller-tower / Lego picture of the Esquisse. Boundary strata are encoded by stable graphs. Their fundamental groupoids are glued from the basic pieces M_{g,n} along clutching/normalisation maps.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The statements are standard once the pinning (rigidification of the dual graph) is understood; without pinning, (a) would fail, since one would get a quotient by Aut(G).

The definition of 'strict' normalisation morphism is not given on this page. From the next page, it means the induced map on full normalisations is an isomorphism. The non-strict case (non-bijective map on vertices/legs, cf. 'S' → S surjectif' on the previous page) is left implicit.
The equation numbering jumps from (133) to (144) on the next page, probably a renumbering slip.

ideas.what: Stratification of the boundary of M̄_{g,n} by stable graphs; the stratum of curves with a given (pinned) dual graph is a product of M_{g_v,n_v} over vertices.
ideas.modern_name: Boundary strata M_Γ ≅ [∏_v M_{g_v,n_v}/Aut Γ]; clutching/gluing morphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford 1969, Knudsen 1983; graph formalism standardised by Kontsevich, Getzler–Kapranov, Arbarello–Cornalba
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the 'structure à l'infini' and the Teichmüller tower, but not in this graph-functorial form

ideas.what: Contravariant functoriality of G ↦ M_G (and of G ↦ Π_1 M_G) under graph normalisation (edge-cutting) morphisms, compatible with disjoint sums (products).
ideas.modern_name: Modular operad / graph-category functoriality of moduli of stable curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Getzler–Kapranov (Modular operads, 1998); Behrend–Manin for stable graphs

ideas.what: Replacing moduli stacks by their fundamental groupoids: Π_1 of a stratum equals the product of Π_1 of the vertex moduli (144); strict normalisations give equivalences.
ideas.modern_name: Profinite Teichmüller groupoid / Teichmüller tower, Lego building blocks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); developed by Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Ihara, Boggi
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (as a programme, without details)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, before Getzler–Kapranov, an explicit functor from a category of stable graphs with normalisation morphisms to stacks (and to fundamental groupoids). It inverts strict morphisms and converts disjoint sums into products. This is essentially the modular-operad structure on {M_{g,n}}, applied to profinite fundamental groupoids.
missed.quote: Ainsi M_G est un foncteur contravariant en G pour les morphismes de normalisation ... Cor Π_1 M_G est un foncteur contravariant en G ... stable
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the operadic/graph-categorical packaging of the Teichmüller tower was present in Grothendieck's own notes, not only the Lego slogan. This is of historical interest for GT-theory and modular operads, though mathematically routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the now-standard stratification of M̄_{g,n} by stable graphs and its functoriality, transported to fundamental groupoids. This is consistent with the Esquisse programme. The explicit functorial graph formalism predates Getzler–Kapranov but is not deep, and much of it is folklore in GT literature.
transcription_corrections: 'des irrégulières stables' is more plausibly 'des graphes stables' or 'en graphes stables' (written above 'morphismes de normalisation').
In (b), the crossed-out text reads roughly 'graphes stables connexes'; the replacement above is again probably 'graphes stables'.
'G la irrégulière somme des G_α' should likely read 'G la graphe somme' or 'G la somme' (disjoint sum) of the G_α.
(133): the original 'M_G → ∏_α M_{G_α}' has 'Π_1' inserted before both sides, i.e. 'Π_1 M_G → ∏_α Π_1 M_{G_α}'.
Marginal NB: approximately 'NB On remplacera ∏M_G par Π_1 M_G ... variante du produit'; the wording is uncertain.
In the Corollary, 'irrégulière stable G' should likely read 'graphe stable G'.
'point, —' is illegible and is probably the start of a sentence, not 'point'.
